summary: Design patterns for building AI agents including ReAct, reflection, planning, and multi-step reasoning

content.overview: AI agent architectures define how agents reason, plan, and act to accomplish goals. The most influential patterns in 2025 are ReAct (Reasoning and Acting), Reflection (self-critique and improvement), and Planning (goal decomposition). These patterns can be combined, with the most effective solutions weaving together tool use, reflection, planning, and adaptive reasoning. Critical insight: Simple architectures (ReAct + Tools) often match complex architectures' accuracy at 50% lower cost.
keyPoints: ReAct Pattern: Iterative loop of Thought (reasoning) → Action (tool call) → Observation (result) → repeat until goal achieved
CRITICAL: ReAct combines chain-of-thought reasoning WITH tool execution in a single loop - not separate phases
Reflection Pattern: Agent evaluates its own outputs, identifies mistakes, and iteratively improves (requires generator + critic components)
Planning Pattern: Decompose complex goals into sequential/parallel subtasks before execution (think first, act later)
Tool Calling Integration: Modern agents drive real outcomes by interacting with APIs, databases, and external systems - not just generating text
COST-ACCURACY TRADEOFF: Simple ReAct + Tools architectures often achieve 90%+ accuracy of complex multi-agent systems at 50% cost
Effective 2025 architectures combine patterns: Tool use + Reflection + Planning + Multi-agent collaboration as needed

examples.title: ReAct Loop Structure
examples.code:
// Iteration 1:
Thought: "I need to find the current weather"
Action: CallTool("weather_api", {location: "NYC"})
Observation: "72°F, sunny"

// Iteration 2:
Thought: "I have the weather. Task complete."
Action: Finish("The weather in NYC is 72°F and sunny")
examples.explanation: ReAct interleaves reasoning and action - each thought informs the next action, each observation informs the next thought

examples.title: Reflection Pattern
examples.explanation: Reflection uses self-critique to catch and correct errors through iterative refinement

warnings: Over-architecting agents adds cost and latency - start simple (ReAct) and add complexity only when needed
Reflection requires additional LLM calls (generator + critic) - often doubles cost, only use when quality justifies expense
Unbounded ReAct loops can exceed context limits or run indefinitely - ALWAYS implement max iteration limits and exit conditions
Planning without execution is useless; execution without planning is chaotic - balance based on task complexity
Tool calling failures cascade through agent workflows - implement robust error handling and fallback strategies
bestPractices: Start with ReAct + Tools for most use cases - 90%+ accuracy at lowest cost
Add Reflection ONLY for tasks requiring high accuracy where errors are costly (legal docs, medical info, financial analysis)
Implement Planning for complex multi-step tasks where upfront decomposition improves efficiency
Set max iterations (typically 5-10) to prevent runaway loops and control costs
Log all thoughts, actions, and observations for debugging and transparency
Design modular tool interfaces - agents should compose tools, not be tightly coupled to specific APIs
